items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: So he decided to come home and join us in the Orleans with Lee Collins and Earl Humphrey's band. That was our band.

ctx.x: All right, now, we're talking to Earl Humphrey. Today is November 30th, 1968. Now, could you tell us about when you were playing with Buddy Petit? What is all you can remember about Buddy Petit?

Well, I suppose it must have been just about 1926. And we had a gig over in Mandeville every other Saturday night. In the hotel. Buddy was stationed over there with another man. And it looks as though he had gotten tired of being over there, kind of lonesome, just working on weekends. So he decided to come home and join us in the Orleans with Lee Collins and Earl Humphrey's band. That was our band. So you mean you had two companies? We only had one until Buddy joined us. So Buddy, he got on the train. We wasn't…
Tell me, what's George Lewis in that band?

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: me and Lee Collins did? We went over there to Mandeville. We played over there at the hotel. Me and Lee had the very name. We played for the hotel over there.

ctx.x: Not anymore. He's one you can say he doesn't drink anymore. Yeah, he ain't been a moment.

I think it, man, you know what me and Lee Collins did? We went over there to Mandeville. We played over there at the hotel. Me and Lee had the very name. We played for the hotel over there. Every Saturday night, you know, during the summer session. Contract. When our buddies over there played with a fella named... He played bass violin. He had him and the Fritz brothers. E Flatt was his name?

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: that was a bad consist of Roy Evans, Son Handy, Lee College, myself, Joe Rovershow.

ctx.x: I mean, why he got off it, I don't know. Uh-huh. And, uh, that was a bad consist of Roy Evans, Son Handy, Lee College, myself, Joe Rovershow. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. So that'd be one of the greatest band you'll play around here. I'll do his name, and I'll see if I can think his name now. I call him Plectum, because he had one of them Plectum guitars. Five-string guitars. Banders, now. What is that little fella's name, man? He turned out to be one of the greatest, he's New York…
Yeah. Well, he had a couple of them, he had Rene Hall and he had Rene Hall. Rene Hall, that's it, that's it.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Me and Lee Collins. With Brother Petit in the truck with us. Playing that sucker.

ctx.x: Yeah, Third and Willa. That's where National Park was. Third and Willa. Well, the game was up at, uh, B-San Park. We was playing... B-San Giants was playing coffee leads. Oh, man, the baseball players all on the back of the truck and everything, you know. Soil dust and everything. We made a round. And... Running the kid's ring there. He's appetizing down there for cooperatives hall or something. Well, we... That's when we were going to stop and buck a little bit. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. He ain't going to pass Lee…
